History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old man with known asthma presents with 3 hours of chest tightness, mild dyspnea, cough, and wheeze after a recent upper-respiratory infection; likely viral-triggered asthma exacerbation worsened by 1-week lapse in inhaler use.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Tight chest for ~3 hours.  
• Course: Began suddenly today; progressively bothersome but no acute deterioration at rest.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild shortness of breath, non-productive cough, wheeze. Feels slightly worse climbing stairs; not breathless at rest. Cough marginally worse at night. No chest pain.  
• Recent illness: Had a cold last week with sore throat and runny nose; cold symptoms improving except persistent cough.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified; has no current reliever inhaler available.  
• Review of systems (pertinent):  
  – ENT: Runny nose last week, sore throat resolved.  
  – Respiratory: Wheeze, dyspnea on exertion, no sputum.  
  – Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.  
  – General: No light-headedness reported.  
  – Other systems: Not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – on regular inhaled corticosteroid (Clenil Modulite) and PRN SABA (salbutamol); last severe exacerbation age 16–17 requiring intubation/hospitalization.  
• Hay fever / allergic rhinitis.  
• Childhood eczema (resolved).  
• Childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).

Medications:
• Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; out of supply for ~1 week.  
• Clenil Modulite (beclomethasone) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented; out of supply for ~1 week.  
• New prescription planned: oral steroids (unspecified preparation, “2 tablets in the morning for 5 days” – exact dose/strength/route not documented).  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.  
• Environmental: Dust.

Social History:
• University student; currently away at university (missed medication refill).  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed.

Family History:
• Mother – eczema.  
• Father – asthma.

Physical Examination:
No in-person examination performed; no vitals available (remote consultation).

Investigations:
None performed or available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation likely precipitated by viral URI and lapse in maintenance therapy.  
  • Prescribe/re-issue Salbutamol inhaler (reliever).  
  • Prescribe/re-issue Clenil Modulite inhaler (preventer).  
  • Educate on regular ICS use and PRN SABA.  
  • Provide spacer device with instructions.  
  • Start short course oral steroids: 2 tablets each morning for 5 days (dose not recorded).  
  • Red-flag advice: seek medical attention if Ventolin required > q3h, worsening SOB at rest, chest tightness/pain, light-headedness.  
  • Recommend rest; patient may self-certify first 7 days off work.  
  • Arrange electronic prescription delivery within 1 hour.  
  • Follow-up: Contact clinician if no improvement or any deterioration.

General Plan items: None additional.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Physical exam, vitals, smoking/alcohol history, detailed medication doses/strengths, allergy reconciliation of non-drug allergens vs. drug list.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional minor audio dropouts but context preserved.
